title: Critique a user flow
prompt:
Review this user flow with a product designer lens.

1. Restate the job-to-be-done in one sentence.
2. Call out friction points that add cognitive load, dead ends, or trust risk.
3. Suggest 3 concrete improvements ranked by impact vs. effort.
4. Note any accessibility or mobile constraints I should not ignore.

Keep feedback specific to the screens and copy shown — avoid generic advice.

title: Explore alternate layouts
prompt:
Given this screen, propose 3 distinct layout directions that preserve the same goals and content hierarchy.

For each direction:
- Name the concept in 3–5 words
- Describe the visual hierarchy and primary CTA placement
- Call out what this direction optimizes for (speed, clarity, delight, density)
- List tradeoffs

Do not default to a card grid. Prefer purposeful composition.

title: Write a component spec
prompt:
Turn this UI into an implementation-ready component spec.

Include:
- Purpose and when to use / not use
- Anatomy (parts and slots)
- Variants and states (default, hover, focus, disabled, error, loading)
- Content rules and truncation behavior
- Accessibility: roles, keyboard, focus order, announcements
- Token / spacing notes (prefer semantic tokens over raw values)
- Empty, overflow, and edge cases

Write for engineers — precise, scannable, no fluff.

title: Accessibility review pass
prompt:
Run an accessibility review of this design.

Check:
- Color contrast for text and interactive states
- Focus visibility and keyboard path
- Touch target size and spacing
- Labels, error messaging, and helper text
- Motion: reduce-motion considerations
- Screen reader naming for icons and custom controls

Return findings as severity-ranked issues with a suggested fix for each.

title: Name components & tokens
prompt:
Propose clear naming for the components, variants, and tokens in this design.

Guidelines:
- Prefer purpose over appearance (e.g. action/primary, not blue-button)
- Keep names consistent with existing system language where possible
- Separate component API from visual style tokens
- Flag anything that looks like a one-off that should become a pattern

Output a table: current label → proposed name → rationale.

title: Design empty & error states
prompt:
Design the empty, loading, and error states for this screen.

For each state:
- What the user needs to understand
- Primary recovery action
- Tone of voice for microcopy (clear, calm, specific)
- What not to hide (e.g. navigation, context)

Keep visual noise low; one message, one action.

title: Visual design critique
prompt:
Critique the visual design of this screen.

Focus on:
- Hierarchy and rhythm
- Spacing consistency
- Type scale and line length
- Color roles (surface, text, accent, feedback)
- Alignment and optical balance

Give 5 prioritized notes. Each note: observation → why it matters → suggested change.

title: Structure a Figma file
prompt:
Recommend a clean Figma file structure for this feature.

Cover:
- Page / section organization
- Cover + changelog expectations
- Component vs. instance usage
- Annotation layer for eng handoff
- How to show responsive / platform variants
- What belongs in the design system vs. local to the file

Optimize for a team that reviews in async critique.
